summary:
What if astronauts could explore Mars with an intelligent navigation system that helps them understand the terrain, avoid potential hazards, and safely accomplish their scientific missions?

MARS-NAV is a web-based Mission Control and navigation platform designed to support future human exploration of Mars. Our project addresses the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge by bringing together NASA scientific data, interactive Martian maps, terrain analysis, and intelligent route planning into one integrated system.

By combining Martian surface imagery, elevation data, geological information, and mission simulations, MARS-NAV helps explorers visualize their surroundings, identify potential risks, plan efficient exploration routes, and estimate the resources needed for their journey.

Our goal is to transform complex NASA data into an accessible decision-support tool that makes future Mars exploration safer, smarter, and more scientifically productive.
details:
About MARS-NAV

MARS-NAV is an interactive Martian exploration platform designed to assist astronauts and mission controllers in planning and simulating surface exploration activities.

The application focuses on Jezero Crater, a scientifically significant region explored by NASA's Perseverance rover.

Through a centralized Mission Control Dashboard, users can explore Martian terrain, view scientific information, select destinations, evaluate potential hazards, and compare possible exploration routes.

The platform also incorporates an Extravehicular Activity (EVA) simulation that models astronaut movement, travel duration, resource consumption, and mission progress.

Rather than functioning as a conventional map, MARS-NAV demonstrates how planetary science data can be transformed into meaningful navigation and mission-planning information.

Key Features

1. Interactive Martian Map

An interactive map of Jezero Crater that allows users to explore the Martian surface, visualize geographic features, and identify potential scientific destinations.

2. NASA Scientific Data Integration

A layered geospatial interface designed to combine multiple types of NASA planetary data, including optical imagery, topographic elevation, and geological observations.

3. Intelligent Route Planning

A route-planning system designed around the A* pathfinding algorithm to compare possible exploration paths based on travel distance, terrain slope, and estimated hazards.

4. Terrain Hazard Analysis

Terrain analysis tools that evaluate elevation changes, steep slopes, uncertain areas, and other potential navigation challenges.

5. Astronaut EVA Simulation

A mission simulation that demonstrates astronaut movement, estimated oxygen consumption, battery usage, travel duration, and return planning.

6. Scientific Exploration Planning

Tools for selecting scientific destinations, organizing exploration objectives, and documenting observations during simulated surface missions.

Tech Stack

Frontend

  • React.js with TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • OpenLayers for interactive mapping
  • Zustand for state management
  • Recharts for dashboard visualizations
  • Lucide React for interface icons

Backend

  • Python with FastAPI
  • PostgreSQL with PostGIS
  • SQLAlchemy
  • NumPy and Rasterio for geospatial processing
  • A* Pathfinding Algorithm
  • RESTful APIs

Deployment

  • Vercel — Frontend hosting
  • Render — Backend hosting
  • PostgreSQL — Mission and geospatial data storage

Innovation Highlights

Unified Martian Exploration Map

MARS-NAV brings together different scientific datasets into a centralized interface, allowing mission planners to examine terrain and scientific locations without switching between multiple mapping tools.

Safety-Oriented Navigation

Instead of focusing only on the shortest distance, the route planner is designed to consider terrain difficulty, potential hazards, and mission constraints when comparing exploration paths.

Intelligent Mission Planning

The platform combines geospatial analysis and route optimization to support informed navigation decisions during simulated Mars surface exploration.

Astronaut Mission Simulation

MARS-NAV demonstrates how travel time, estimated resource consumption, mission objectives, and return-route planning can be monitored in a unified dashboard.

Science-Driven Exploration

Scientific destinations can be integrated into route planning, helping users balance exploration goals with estimated travel requirements and terrain risks.

Human-Centered Design

Complex planetary information is presented through an intuitive Mission Control Dashboard designed to make scientific data easier to understand and use.
